data.title: Parapsoriasis — viva
data.summary: Papulosquamous & erythroderma · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Parapsoriasis** (Papulosquamous & erythroderma)_

**Q1. What does 'parapsoriasis' mean today?**
- Group of chronic, scaly, psoriasis-like but treatment-resistant dermatoses described by Brocq (1902)
- Current use: small-plaque parapsoriasis (SPP) and large-plaque parapsoriasis (LPP); pityriasis lichenoides (PLEVA/PLC) were formerly called 'parapsoriasis guttata/varioliformis' and are now classified separately

**Q2. Describe small-plaque parapsoriasis.**
- Round/oval, well-defined, slightly scaly, pink-yellowish patches <5 cm on trunk and proximal limbs of middle-aged men
- Digitate dermatosis variant — finger-like elongated patches along skin lines of the flanks ('hug sign')
- Benign course; rarely (≈ 0–10%) progresses to mycosis fungoides; some regard it as abortive MF

**Q3. Describe large-plaque parapsoriasis.**
- Patches >5 cm, irregular, on 'bathing-trunk' area (buttocks, hips, thighs), breasts, flexures; mild scaling and itch
- Poikilodermatous variant (atrophy, telangiectasia, mottled pigmentation — 'poikiloderma vasculare atrophicans')
- Progresses to mycosis fungoides in ~10–30% (some say it is patch-stage MF) — needs long-term follow-up and repeated biopsies

**Q4. How do you differentiate parapsoriasis from early mycosis fungoides?**
- Clinically difficult; MF suspected with progressive size >5 cm, poikiloderma, sun-protected distribution, plaques/infiltration, persistent itch
- Histology: MF shows epidermotropism of atypical cerebriform lymphocytes without much spongiosis, Pautrier microabscesses, lymphocytes lined along the basal layer; immunohistochemistry (CD4>CD8, loss of CD7) and TCR gene rearrangement (clonality)

**Q5. Differential diagnosis.**
- Psoriasis, nummular eczema, pityriasis rosea (self-limiting), tinea corporis, drug eruption, pityriasis lichenoides chronica, MF, secondary syphilis, seborrhoeic dermatitis

**Q6. Treatment.**
- SPP: emollients, topical steroids, NB-UVB (most effective), PUVA; can be left alone with follow-up
- LPP: phototherapy (NB-UVB/PUVA), potent topical steroids, topical nitrogen mustard/bexarotene; biopsy any change
- Follow-up every 6–12 months (LPP) for MF transformation

**Q7. What is pityriasis lichenoides?**
- Spectrum of clonal T-cell lymphoproliferative inflammatory disorders: PLEVA (Mucha–Habermann — acute crops of papules with haemorrhagic crusts/necrosis healing with varioliform scars; febrile ulceronecrotic variant is an emergency) and PLC (chronic red-brown papules with mica-like scale that peels off)
- Histology: interface dermatitis with wedge-shaped infiltrate, extravasated RBCs, necrotic keratinocytes
- Treatment: erythromycin/doxycycline, NB-UVB, methotrexate for severe

**Q8. Describe the staging of mycosis fungoides (because LPP may evolve).**
- TNMB staging (ISCL/EORTC): T1 patches/plaques <10% BSA, T2 ≥10%, T3 tumours, T4 erythroderma; nodes, viscera, blood (Sézary cells) — stages IA–IVB; early stages (IA–IIA) have near-normal life expectancy

**Q9. What is the treatment of early mycosis fungoides?**
- Skin-directed: topical steroids, nitrogen mustard (mechlorethamine gel), bexarotene gel, imiquimod; NB-UVB (patches) or PUVA (plaques), local radiotherapy; advanced — total skin electron beam, interferon-α, bexarotene, methotrexate, mogamulizumab, brentuximab (CD30+), ECP, HDAC inhibitors, allogeneic transplant

## Quick spotter facts
- Finger-like patches on flanks — digitate dermatosis (SPP)
- Large poikilodermatous patches in bathing-trunk area — LPP, watch for MF

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Parapsoriasis; cutaneous lymphoma). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
